speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI) with septic arthritis of the wrist and tenosynovitis. The history of recent camping, sexually active status, triad of migratory polyarthralgia, monoarticular arthritis, and fever is classic for DGI. REQUEST TEST: Blood Cultures, Synovial Fluid Analysis, RPR/VDRL. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray Left Wrist.
